title: quercus peduncularis subsp. eupeduncularis
intro: Quercus peduncularis subsp. eupeduncularis, commonly known as the Korean pedunculate oak, is a subspecies of oak tree native to East Asia, characterized by its distinctive pedunculate acorns. It is valued for its potential health benefits, including its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which may help to protect against chronic diseases and promote wound healing. The therapeutic actions of Quercus peduncularis subsp. eupeduncularis are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins, which have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities. Research on the plant's bioactive constituents is ongoing, but preliminary findings suggest that it may have potential as a natural remedy for various health conditions.
